title: Microboarding: 15-day personalized onboarding sprint and hiring/rubric templates
body:
Purpose:
A compact, repeatable 15-day microboarding sprint for ICs and new managers that pairs a minimal hiring plan template and interview rubric. Goal: get a new hire to shipping-confidence for a single priority within 15 days (not fully productive — narrow scope). This doc bundles: a preboarding checklist, a day-by-day sprint, a lightweight hiring plan snapshot, and a 3-axis interview rubric to reduce hiring variance.

Context / why this exists:
- People ops + hiring velocity: many teams want a faster, lower-friction onboarding path for small pods and fast-moving projects.
- We observed long first-30-day ramp times caused by diffuse goals, missing access, and overloaded first-week schedules. Microboarding reduces cognitive load and aligns expectations.
- Complement to existing 30/60/90 playbooks (this is intentionally narrow and iterative).

Who should use it:
- Hiring manager + buddy for early-stage hires (IC-I to IC-III)
- People Ops when scoping offers and creating a focused 15-day success plan
- Recruiting when evaluating candidates against a pragmatic rubric for immediate contribution roles

Quick TL;DR checklist (preboarding):
- Offer signed: confirm start date and time zone, send welcome email + 15-day sprint doc.
- Access: email, Redwood VPN, Slack, GitHub org invite, CI test account, Console read-only token for team project.
- Hardware: laptop provisioned and imaged, accessories shipped, asset ticket created.
- First task assigned: a single onboarding ticket (bugfix or doc) with clear acceptance criteria.
- Buddy + manager assigned and calendar blocked for 1:1 (15m/day first week).
- Team quick-read: 10-15 slide deck with codebase overview + runbook links.
- Learning path: 2 short videos (10–15m) and 1 small repo clone exercise.

Microboarding 15-day schedule (scoped, repeatable):
- Day 0 (pre-day): confirm access + hardware; send "what to expect" email with short sprint goals.
- Day 1: orientation + environment setup: small guided repo clone + run unit tests; lunch intro with buddy; assign onboarding ticket (25% of sprint).
- Day 2: first small PR (fix or doc) — aim to merge; manager review; 15m check-in.
- Day 3: pair on a slightly larger task (40% of sprint) — focus on understanding architecture slice.
- Day 4: async deep-dive: read 1 design doc + leave 3 clarification comments; update onboarding ticket.
- Day 5: Friday demo: short show-and-tell of week progress; manager gives targeted feedback.
- Day 6–8 (week 2 start): ramp to independent task (60–80% of sprint); focus on shipping a small feature or reliable improvement.
- Day 9: mid-sprint feedback loop with people ops + manager (15 min) — confirm signals.
- Day 10–12: polish, tests, documentation, deploy to staging.
- Day 13: cross-team review / seek one L3 reviewer for knowledge share.
- Day 14: final review + prepare short write-up of what was shipped and next steps.
- Day 15: celebration + 30-minute retro with buddy + manager; map next 30-day objective.

Acceptance criteria for the 15-day sprint (example):
- Code is merged into main or a documented follow-up exists.
- Automated tests added or existing flakiness addressed.
- A short doc (<= 500 words) explains the change and where to look.
- New hire can explain the architecture slice to the buddy in <10 minutes.
- Manager and buddy both mark "green" on readiness checklist.

Lightweight hiring plan snapshot (for roles using microboarding):
- Role tag: backend-engineer-small-team
- Hiring priority: speed-to-first-ship (3–6 weeks goal)
- Must-haves: core systems debugging, Git workflow, unit tests, service ownership mindset
- Scorecard summary (used by recruiting): technical fundamentals (40%), collaboration (20%), product sense (15%), learning velocity (15%), cultural fit (10%)
- Interview loop suggestion: 3 rounds + take-home (or paired coding in loop):
  1) Recruiter screen (30m) — culture + logistics
  2) Manager + hiring peer (45m) — system design micro (15–20m) + behavioral + ownership questions
  3) Pair + coding (60m) — real repo/mini-feature or focused kata with pairing; aim for mergeable PR within follow-up tasks
  4) Optional: take-home for complex roles (48–72h)

Interview rubric (3-axis simplified template — keep small to reduce noise):
- Axis 1: Correctness & Fundamentals (0–4)
  - 0: severe gaps in basic problem solving, incorrect assumptions, or cannot write runnable pseudocode.
  - 2: some correct approach but sloppy or requires heavy guidance.
  - 4: clear, correct, efficient solution; anticipates edge cases; tests considered.
- Axis 2: Ownership & Product Sense (0–4)
  - 0: no sense of impact or prioritization, ignores tradeoffs.
  - 2: demonstrates basic ownership; can articulate tradeoffs with prompting.
  - 4: proactive ownership examples, clear impact quantification, proposes sensible tradeoffs.
- Axis 3: Collaboration & Communication (0–4)
  - 0: poor communication; cannot explain approach.
  - 2: communicates clearly with occasional clarifying questions; receptive to feedback.
  - 4: excellent communication, explains tradeoffs clearly, invites feedback and writes clean PR descriptions.
- Guidance: hire if average >= 2.7 and no axis is 0. Use comments to call out biggest risk areas.

First-15-day manager checklist (short):
- Day 0: send welcome + sprint doc; schedule daily 1:1s (first week) and weekly afterwards.
- Provide clear priority: one shipable item.
- Confirm buddy has time for pairing on Days 1–3.
- Reserve code review capacity so PRs are not blocked >48h.
- Give frequent, specific feedback (what's working / one small change).

Buddy checklist (short):
- Day 1: 30–60m pairing on local setup + small task.
- Days 2–5: be available for quick pairing and code reviews (aim <24h).
- End of week: prep lightweight demo and help write the 500-word explainer.

Risk signals to surface early (trigger people ops/manager action):
- No access to critical systems after Day 1 (escalate to infra).
- Repeated blocker >48h on PRs or environment issues.
- New hire unable to describe the change or fails simple tests after Day 5 — schedule calibration and remediation plan.

Metrics to track (minimal):
- Merge within 15 days (binary).
- Time-to-first-PR (days).
- New hire self-rating on readiness (Day 5 and Day 15).
- Buddy/manager readiness score (Day 15).

Notes / questions / TODOs (raw):
- Q: Should we require a mandatory take-home for backend-mid roles? Tradeoff: predictability vs. bias and time cost.
- TODO: build a Confluence template that auto-populates role, manager, and repo links (linked_artifacts above is a seed).
- TODO: add a simple calendar template (Day1–Day5 timeblocks) for managers.
- Consider an A/B test: microboarding vs. classic 30-day for 20 hires and measure retention & time-to-first-merge.

Appendix: example micro-hiring ad (short):
- "Backend Engineer — small pod. First 15 days focused on shipping a reliability improvement. Join us if you like small-scope ownership, quick iteration, and working with a supportive buddy system."

Contact: Asha Kapoor (people ops), slack: #people-ops-onboarding, ping @asha for clarifying questions.

End of doc.
